When use: Use when the summary mentions the wrong person, participant, entity, name, or object, or introduces an entity not supported by the source dialogue.
Use when the summary adds, changes, or fabricates an event/action that is not supported by the source dialogue.
Use when the event is roughly correct, but the participant roles are wrong, such as who did the action, who received it, or who said it.
Use when the summary gets circumstantial details wrong, such as time, place, number, quantity, condition, or schedule.
Use when the summary changes negation, uncertainty, intention, obligation, or modality, such as “might” becoming “will,” or “did not” becoming “did.”
Use when the summary misrepresents the discourse relation or final outcome, such as cause-effect, contrast, temporal order, decision, agreement, or conclusion.
Use when the summary misses a salient event, participant, reason, decision, or final outcome that is important for understanding the dialogue.
Use when the output has language, translation, fluency, formatting, or instruction-following issues, such as English leakage, malformed Chinese, repeated text, or non-summary output.
